'''Ubagami Daijingū Togyo Festival''' (姥神大神宮渡御祭) is the grand festival (例大祭) of [[:en:Hokkaidō|Hokkaido's]] oldest shrine, [[Ubagami Daijingū]] ({{ill|Ubagami Daijingū|fr|Ubagami Daijin-gū|ja|姥神大神宮|qid=Q3547609|lt=Ubagami Daijingū}}), located in [[Esashi, Hiyama District, Hokkaido|Esashi Town, Hiyama District]].

== Overview ==

The event includes a [[Mikoshi]] procession followed by parade floats (referred to as "Yama" in the town), which travel through the town. == History ==
The festival’s origins are unclear, but common belief ties it to the year {{ill|1644|en|1644|qid=Q6920|lt=1644}} ({{ill|Shōhō|en|Shōhō|qid=Q1146192|lt=Shōhō}} 1), when Ubagami Daijingū was relocated to its current site<ref>{{Sfn|Festival Record|1999|page=10}}</ref>.

يىلى|uk|1816|ur|1816ء|uz|1816|vec|1816|vi|1816|vls|1816|vo|1816|wa|1816|war|1816|wuu|1816年|xmf|1816|yi|1816|zea|1816|zh|1816年|zh_min_nan|1816 nî|zh_yue|1816年|qid=Q6953|lt=1816}} ({{ill|Culture|en|Culture|qid=Q11042|lt=Bunka}} 13), records from the Fujieda family in the document “Shrine Grounds Chronicle”<ref>{{Sfn|Festival Record|1999|page=10}}</ref> state that the festival alternated yearly between Ubagami Daijingū and Benten Shrine on [[Kamome Island, Esashi|Kamome Island]] (present-day {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine (Kamome Island)|ja|厳島神社 (江差町)}}) during August 14–16. يىلى|uk|1962|ur|1962ء|uz|1962|vec|1962|vi|1962|vls|1962|vo|1962|wa|1962|war|1962|wuu|1962年|xmf|1962|yi|1962|za|1962 nienz|zea|1962|zh|1962年|zh_classical|一九六二年|zh_min_nan|1962 nî|zh_yue|1962年|qid=Q2764|lt=1962}} (Showa 37), the festival dates were August 20–23 but were changed to the current schedule through a town-wide survey<ref>{{Sfn|Festival Record|1999|page=12}}</ref>.

== Floats ("Yama") ==
In Esashi, the parade floats are referred to as "Yama" and are cherished by each neighborhood. The floats follow the mikoshi procession. This practice began in the mid-19th century and continues to this day<ref>{{Sfn|Ubagami Daijingū Festival Photo Collection|2002|pages=110-111}}</ref>.

The oldest float is Jingū Yama’s figure of {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|qid=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}}, crafted in {{ill|Hōreki|en|Hōreki|qid=Q1194397|lt=Hōreki}} 4 (1754). It is a designated Tangible Folk Cultural Property of Hokkaido.

Floats like Seimu Yama feature unique karakuri mechanisms that allow movement. Matsuhōmaru, the only "ship float," is built in the style of a traditional Japanese ship.

For more information, visit the [https://esashi.town/tourism Ubakami Festival Website].
